notes: §1985:VI.4.4.2 prints the header OBJECT-COMPUTER and its period, then one bracket holding computer-name, an optional MEMORY SIZE integer-1 with WORDS, CHARACTERS or MODULES, an optional PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1 and the second period (printed page VI-11 rendered: MEMORY, the three units and SEQUENCE are the underlined words, and the period stands inside the bracket). Implemented at 85: objectComputerParagraph takes the header alone or a computer-name and clauses; memorySizeClause (left-edge predicate memorySizeAhead) requires an integer literal and one of the three units with SIZE optional; programCollatingSequenceClause takes SEQUENCE with PROGRAM, COLLATING and IS optional, and SpecialNamesBinder.ResolveProgramCollating binds the alphabet; VersionConformancePass.VisitObjectComputerParagraph refuses a clause with no computer-name below 2002 (COBOL0900), VisitProgramCollatingSequenceClause the second alphabet-name and the FOR forms, VisitCharacterClassificationClause that clause, while VisitMemorySizeClause admits MEMORY SIZE below 2002; the 1985 arm of the ClauseCardinalities row (ByClauseContext) has ClosedFormatPass.ScreenClauseRepetition refuse a repeated clause (COBOL2423) and SEQUENCE before MEMORY (COBOL2987); ScreenParagraphPeriods refuses a missing closing period (COBOL3408); IntegerOperandPass.VisitIntegerLiteral refuses integer-1 of zero, which §1985:III requires ("it must be neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed by the rules for that format"). Missing, as on 1985-FMT-VI.4.3.2: the grammar's final period is optional whatever precedes it and ScreenParagraphPeriods returns when ParagraphPeriods.Sentences finds no sentence, so OBJECT-COMPUTER followed by two periods and no computer-name is accepted at 85; that is the 2023 spelling (§2023:12.3.6.2, §2023:12.3.6.3 SR4), and the 1985 bracket gives the second period only with a computer-name. The witness writes a name, MEMORY SIZE 4096 WORDS and a collating sequence that reverses a comparison. Probed at --std 85: the empty paragraph, a name, each unit, MEMORY without SIZE, SEQUENCE alone, both clauses in the printed order, and SEGMENT-LIMIT after them are accepted; MEMORY SIZE with no unit, a unit BYTES, two units, a signed, decimal, zero or data-name integer-1, the clauses reversed, either clause twice, a clause without a name, a period between the name and a clause, a literal alphabet, an undeclared alphabet, COLLATING without SEQUENCE, CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION, two alphabet-names, FOR ALPHANUMERIC, a computer named MEMORY, and a missing closing period are refused.

[ computer-name [MEMORY SIZE integer-1 {WORDS|CHARACTERS|MODULES}] [PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS alphabet-name-1] . ]: the clauses need computer-name. §2023:12.3.6.2 writes [ computer-name-1 ] and the CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION and PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses (with FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL) as independent options, and has no MEMORY SIZE clause; §2023:12.3.6.3 SR4: "If neither computer-name-1 nor any of the optional clauses is specified, the second period in the General format may be omitted." A 1985 program with MEMORY SIZE is refused; clauses without computer-name are newly accepted. Compile-time only.
